h: Hotspur's home and the coast around it
p: Warkworth was a favourite home of the powerful Percy family, and its most famous resident was Harry Hotspur, the fiery young lord who rebelled against Henry IV and died at the Battle of Shrewsbury in 1403. Shakespeare brought him to life in Henry IV, and the castle even features in the play. So if you've got a theatre lover in the group, they'll be in their element.

Allow two to three hours for the castle, then save some time for the village. Down at the other end of the main street, look out for the medieval fortified bridge over the Coquet, complete with its gatehouse tower. Bridges like this are a real rarity, and it's a cracking spot for a photo. The village itself is pretty, with stone houses, tearooms and a good church to poke your head into.

Head towards the sea and you'll find a long sandy beach backed by dunes, perfect for a breezy walk, and the Northumberland Coast Path runs right along this stretch. Just round the corner, Amble is a busy little harbour town with seafood, cafés and the harbour village of small shops. From Amble, seasonal boat trips head out around Coquet Island, an RSPB reserve with puffins, terns and seals. You don't land on the island, but the views from the boat are terrific.
Got a car and some energy left? Alnwick, with its huge castle and the Alnwick Garden, is only a short drive inland, and it makes a fantastic second stop on another day.
